direction: Stagnation-adaptive composite ruin scoring: blend normalized worst-removal savings with a tight-capacity demand/slack term (removal_savings + w_dem * (demand_u / route_load_u) + w_slack * (capacity - route_load_u)/capacity) and a Shaw-style proximity-to-centroid term, then let iter_frac drive a scheduled decay from savings-dominant (early) toward randomness-injected/flat weighting (late) so late LNS escapes Record-to-Record plateaus on tight-capacity, 100-node, eccentric-depot instances instead of repeatedly removing the same worst-cost nodes.

operations.mechanism: Round 6 SBS (15.8948, 230.9 ms) already spends well under the 500 ms budget, so extra per-iteration quality (diversity of ruin choice) is affordable rather than more iterations. Archived weakest regimes are tight capacity (12/24 instances, rel gap -23.2%) and size=100 (12/24, -21.7%), where worst-cost removal repeatedly targets the same few nodes; KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 shows the hook space is wide (L3-ctrl worst-cost baseline beaten by evolved hooks) and method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret / impl-cvrp-xfer-mixed both indicate that blended savings + demand/geometry (and capacity-aware early-return) terms generalize better than a single savings criterion. The stagnation_ratio and iter_frac hook inputs specifically enable the scheduled decay, keeping the single-hook interface intact with postprocess none.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Because the weakest regime is capacity_level=tight (vbs_rel_gap_pct -23.21%) together with size=100 and depot_style=eccentric, pure worst-cost removal over-exploits the same high-savings nodes and stalls; adding a capacity-slack/demand-ratio term and decaying the savings weight with iter_frac will increase ruin diversity per iteration and lower mean objective on dev_24 by >=0.10 (from 15.8948 toward <=15.79) at equal-or-lower solve_ms than the round-6 SBS.
